what: Every resource bound on the path SDK admission -> Torii -> queue -> VM -> proposer -> block -> RS16 payload -> transport, frame and sync -> follower validation -> storage, with its value today, its single code owner, where it is enforced, how it is classed and the relations that must hold between bounds. The checker reads every owner from the source and fails on drift. `completeness` names the owner files, directories and committed-parameter modules the checker scans: a limit defined there is a bound here or is excluded with a reason. `catalogs` checks the node-local validity limits against the three typed catalogs of node configuration the code owns (the execution-policy digest, the ZK consensus-policy hash and the Nexus consensus-policy preimage) and the committed limits against the two committed policy structs. `pin_tests` names the tests that only pin a value or a digest projection: a consensus bound backed by nothing else records the task that owns its boundary test.

classes.consensus: Deterministic consensus bound. Every validator derives the same accept or reject decision from committed State or a compile-time protocol constant. A validity-affecting bound whose source is node-local configuration is a defect with an owning task.
classes.local_defer: Local resource. Exhausting it defers or refuses one local attempt; it never rejects a transaction or block, casts a vote or changes an accepted effect, gas or certified root.
classes.engineering_target: Engineering time or memory target measured on named hardware. It guides construction, is compared with an observation only and is never validity.
classes.local_schedule: Local scheduling limit. A time budget a node plans or waits within, including a committed parameter used that way. Exceeding it retries or re-plans one local attempt; it never rejects a transaction or block, casts a vote or changes an accepted effect, gas or certified root, and it is not a performance target.

sources.committed: Genesis or State parameter; the owner is its default.
sources.node_local: Node configuration or a node-local default.

fields.owner: The single definition the checker reads: file, symbol, kind (const, fn, field or arm), optional anchors applied in order and the defining expression. `refs` maps a constant the expression names to the bound that owns it.
fields.enforcement: Where the bound is compared or applied, by stage. A site that is only a symbol, a constant definition or a function signature is rejected. `count` is how many times the text occurs in the file when that is not one; a different number is drift.
fields.tests: Active Rust or Python tests of the bound (`macro` names a macro_rules! generator, `macro_path` the file that defines it when the test file is an include of it). A test that is ignored, compiled out, without #[test] or in a file no module path of its crate reaches is rejected.
fields.test_gap: The task that owns the missing boundary test of a consensus bound. The bound names no test, or only tests listed in `pin_tests`.
fields.test_note: What the named tests do and do not cover.
fields.unenforced: A value bound into consensus State that no state transition compares anything with; the owner task enforces or removes it. `observations` may name a local service that compares it.
fields.defect: Why a validity-affecting bound read from node configuration is a defect, with its owner task.
fields.catalog: The field of an authoritative typed catalog in the code this node-local bound mirrors.
fields.observations: Where something is compared with the bound outside consensus validity: a measured value as evidence, or the own check of a local service for a bound recorded `unenforced`.
fields.zero_means: What the value zero means for this bound.
fields.inclusive: Whether the bound itself is admitted.
fields.framing: Which encoding overhead a byte length includes.
fields.fixed: The delivery plan keeps this value; the checker holds an independent copy.
fields.value_pin: Why a pin of the value is the right test of a bound whose every test is in `pin_tests`.

stage_decisions.what: How the stages decide on the size of one transaction, from committed parameters only.
stage_decisions.sdk: Parameters::check_signed_transaction_bytes(bytes, route): at most min(max_tx_bytes, the largest selection budget on the route). TransactionInclusionRoute::Global is max_block_bytes - 65,536 and is sufficient on every route; NativeLane { max_block_bytes } adds that lane's max_block_bytes - 64 and holds only for a transaction the committed routing rules send to that lane.
stage_decisions.torii: AcceptedTransaction admission: at most max_tx_bytes; then the queue.
stage_decisions.queue: Queue::prepare_checked_for_enqueue: the bound of the transaction's route at the admission height. A transaction routed to lane zero has the global budget; one routed to a native lane also has the budget of that lane's committed record (the payload limit its proposer builds within, pinned when the lane was created). Above it the transaction is refused as UnsupportedTransactionAdmission with the actual and permitted bytes. An unreadable committed policy or route defers the assessment (Error::Deferred) and takes no custody.
stage_decisions.proposer: payload::select: at most min(max_transactions, FASTPQ Network input cap) own transactions within max_block_bytes - 65,536, including the rescue of an input whose lane has stalled; the lane builder selects within the lane's max_block_bytes - 64 and compares the encoded batch with the lane's max_block_bytes; then the assembled proposal wire within max_block_bytes.
stage_decisions.follower: Signed header payload_len <= max_block_bytes and every transaction <= max_tx_bytes. The follower accepts every block an honest proposer builds. The proposer's reserve is packing policy, not a validity rule: a block around a transaction inside the reserve window is valid if built.
stage_decisions.agreement: Where transaction_cap_fits_block_payload holds, every stage accepts exactly the transactions of at most max_tx_bytes. Where it does not (today's defaults), admission is stricter than block validity by the reserve, so nothing admitted is larger than the selection budget of a proposer on its route at the admission height. That is not a promise of inclusion for a lane-routed transaction above the global budget: only its lane's proposer can carry it. The global rescue selects within the global budget and skips it, so if the lane stalls or closes, or the routing rules stop sending the transaction to that lane, it stays queued until it expires.

ram_lfe.what: Budgets of the full RAM-LFE workload, derived from the candidate shape recorded by the R.0 contract (specs/ram_lfe_execution_proof.md): 64 input slots, 64 outputs, four registers, 32 state lanes, 256 instructions, rank 16, 64 refreshes. Every part of the workload has a budget (`component`): the registered program, key registration, the request, evaluation, the receipt, verification, the single-opener opening, the threshold opening, the validator's decode and verification scratch, each of the three classes, leakage and the prover. A budget whose inputs are all known has a number the checker recomputes. A budget with an open input has no number: its formula and inputs are recorded and the owning task supplies the measurement. Every open input and every shape bound is used by a budget. The standalone IPA diagnostic domain cap is independent of operation-proof admission; the current native PIPA-R payload ceiling (proof.config_pipa_r_max_proof_bytes) does not qualify a new RAM-LFE execution relation.

catalogs.what: The typed catalog of node configuration that decides validity or effects outside [zk] and [nexus]: the function hashes each field into the execution-policy digest committed with State. Two fields are digests of the other two node-configuration catalogs (`digests`), whose fields are classified there. The checker reads the field list from the function, including names a loop takes from a literal table, and fails on a field that is neither or on a field it cannot name.

Admitted signature and hash algorithms: a cryptographic admission policy, not a resource bound.

Governance, citizenship, viral-incentive, SoraFS pin and parliament policy: limits of those products' own registries and schedules. They are node-local validity policy F.4 moves with each product; none bounds the transaction and proof path.

The Nexus fee schedule and its accounts: who is paid and at what rate, not a resource bound. F.3 and F.4 own their committed source.
Timing of shared Hugging Face lease pools and the endorsement committee: a grace period and an identity set with its quorum, not bounds on bytes, counts or work.
AXT expiry timing and replay retention measured in slots: validity windows, not bounds on bytes, counts or work. A.3 and F.4 own them.
The activation switch of atomic private settlement and its notice period: an activation gate. P.5 and F.4 remove runtime activation predicates.

Relation and audit-policy identity of atomic private settlement (proof profile version, permitted policy versions, minimum auditor approvals): which relation and policy apply, not a resource bound. P.20 and F.4 own them.

Validity windows of atomic private settlement measured in blocks (expiry span, audit, prepare and commit timeouts, sidecar retention): windows, not bounds on bytes, counts or work. The expiry span is compared in the same State check as the two listed bounds.

The list of padded capsule plaintext classes: a shape table of four sizes, not one bound. Its largest class (262,144 bytes) is below proof.config_private_settlement_max_capsule_bytes, which is the listed ceiling.
Governance module identities and parameters, the compliance switches and the digests of the loaded compliance and lane-manifest policy sets: which policy applies, not a resource bound.

Lane fusion and autoscale policy and the commit window: load thresholds, lane-id ranges, ratios and windows that schedule lanes. They decide how many lanes exist, not how large a transaction, proof or block may be.

Sampling, audit, recovery and rotation policy of the Nexus DA attester service and the length of the ingest quota window: committee sampling geometry and windows. The RS16 payload availability of consensus blocks is listed under rs16.*, and the two ingest quota ceilings are listed above.

catalogs.what: The committed execution-output policy of a block (BlockParameter::ExecutionOutput). The struct is a committed parameter: every field is a bound of this contract. The checker reads the fields of the struct and fails on a field that is not listed.

The committed FASTPQ source policy of a block (BlockParameter::FastpqSource) with its intrinsic, block and mandatory limit sets. The struct is a committed parameter: every field is a bound of this contract. The checker reads the fields of the struct and fails on a field that is not listed.

completeness.what: The owner files, directories and committed-parameter modules the checker scans. In a `const` scope every constant whose name marks a limit (MAX, MAXIMUM, LIMIT, BUDGET, CEILING, OVERHEAD, RESERVE, CAP or CAPACITY) is in scope; in a `default_fn` scope every default of the module is. A `tree` scope scans every Rust source below a directory, test, bench, example and fixture files and the paths under `skip` excepted, so a new file there is scanned too. Each limit is the owner of a bound above or is excluded here with the reason it is not a resource bound of the transaction and proof path. A new limit in a scanned file fails the checker until it is classified, and every file that owns a constant bound is scanned. The directories are the ones on the path: the transaction, block, proof, parameter and instruction models, the consensus core and its node driver, the pipeline, the IVM and its ABI, and the P2P layer.

scopes.why: The generic proof batch bound is defined directly in zk; nested proof and local-diagnostic modules have their own complete scans.

The Torii module holds the limits of every HTTP service. Only its request-body and query fetch-size limits are scanned: they bound what a client can submit or a contract can read. Connection, rate, cache and service-registry capacities are local serving policy off the transaction path.

skip.why: The deterministic simulator behind the `sim` feature: a test harness that injects loss, delay and faults. It never runs in a node.

excluded.reason: Codec-internal decode guards (archive length, nesting depth, header padding, varint width). Each chain bound above is measured on the framed encoding and is far below them; they never decide admission.
Committee-size geometry (3f + 1 with f <= 10): a protocol structure bound, covered on the transport path by transport.max_committee_size.
Signer bitmap bytes of the largest committee: derived from transport.max_committee_size.

Shape bounds of one privacy product's statement (ZK-ACE accounts and policies, nullifier and commitment counts of one action). They are inside the action bytes proof.privacy_max_action_bytes bounds; P.4 and the product tasks own their relations.
A decoder-internal field ceiling derived from a listed payload bound (the proof-box and verifying-key payload ceilings) plus its length prefix; it admits nothing the listed bound refuses.
Shape bounds of the Ed25519 batch-verification opcode payload, inside the guest memory and gas budgets; M.1 inventories the opcode's semantics.
Connection, send-queue and gossip fan-out capacity of the P2P layer: local back-pressure that delays or drops a delivery. It bounds no frame, transaction or block.
Largest number of transactions in one gossip batch: a local delivery batch size. The frame that carries the batch is bounded by transport.max_frame_bytes_tx_gossip.
QUIC datagram size of the optional transport: a path-MTU setting below every frame bound; frames above it use streams.
Per-topic frame caps defined as transport.max_plaintext_frame_bytes itself; that bound and relation driver_frame_limit_within_transport_cap cover them.
Frame caps of topics that carry no transaction, proof or block: peer gossip, health, Connect relay and miscellaneous control traffic.
Capacity of a local cache. A miss recomputes; it never changes a verdict. The retained-byte budget of the same caches is decoded_scratch.ivm_cache_max_bytes.
Batch size of local signature verification: a performance setting with identical results at any size.
Local FASTPQ prover sidecar queue, retry and GPU settings: they bound a node's own proving pipeline, not what a transaction or block may carry.
A validity window in blocks, not a bound on bytes, counts or work; excluded from catalog zk_consensus_policy_hash for the same reason. F.4 owns validity windows.
A validity window in blocks, not a bound on bytes, counts or work; excluded from catalog zk_consensus_policy_hash for the same reason. F.4 owns validity windows.

A per-route HTTP body limit below the proxy ceiling transport.torii_max_content_len. Relation torii_body_carries_max_transaction is stated on the ceiling; the per-route defaults are local serving limits X.2 measures with the maximum envelope.

zk-X509 relation geometry and private-witness shape (trace size, constraint degree, FRI parameters, DER field maxima, sub-proof frame sizes). They are prover-side construction parameters whose transported result is bounded by x509.max_proof_bytes and x509.max_encoded_x5s1_bytes; X.3 owns them and the q=136 reduction.

Statement-shape or registry-capacity bound of one privacy product (anonymous PGC, VeRange, ZK-AMS, Jindo, Bootle-Lantern, Vega, Orchard, FCMP++, IVM private notes, PQ-MASP and the zk-X509 certificate, attribute, trust-anchor, policy and CRL-lineage shapes). A shape bound lies inside the action bytes proof.privacy_max_action_bytes bounds or in the private witness, which never travels; a registry capacity bounds that product's committed State. P.4, X.3 and the product tasks own them. The zk-X509 chain depth, CRL age and presentation window in this file are listed bounds.
The sum of the listed data and parity shard maxima (rs16.max_data_shards and rs16.max_parity_shards): a derived geometry constant.
The public u64 form of the listed rs16.max_payload_size_bytes, whose owner is the private MAX_DA_PAYLOAD_SIZE in the same file.
An associated constant of the bounded-frame trait that names the listed frame bound of its type (rs16.max_availability_frame_bytes and the availability table bounds).
Largest local view timeout: a pacemaker timer bound, not a resource bound.
Size of the fixed-layout result preimage of the commit certificate: part of the certificate, not of the proposal payload; transport.frame_overhead_bytes accounts for the certificate.
A re-export of block.max_executed_block_wire_bytes, whose owner is crates/iroha_data_model/src/block/consensus.rs.
Age thresholds of the local queue-pressure heuristic: they change when a node sheds load, never whether a transaction is valid.
Program-header field ranges and the debug-section decode allocation: metadata shape bounds inside guest_memory.max_program_image_bytes; the debug section is never executed.
A decode-limit structure assembled from the listed program-image and decode-allocation bounds; it defines no value of its own.
Shape bounds of the typed call ABI (schema nodes, depth, table and word counts). The frame they describe is bounded by guest_memory.max_call_frame_bytes; M.1 inventories them.

Shape bounds of the durable-state syscalls (path, key, page and scan sizes) and the decimal scale. The value they read or write is bounded by decoded_scratch.state_max_value_bytes; M.1 inventories each syscall.
A syscall number, not a limit; the name contains a limit word.
Shape bound of one host syscall family (NFT enumeration, spend frames) inside the guest memory and gas budgets listed above; M.1 inventories each syscall's semantics.
Lane-autoscale bookkeeping in committed State (committee record bytes and sample history): it bounds the autoscaler's own state, not a transaction, proof or block.

Committed-State capacity of one product (VPN settlement receipts, the standalone election ballot corpus, threshold-key lifecycle state). Each bounds that product's own State; the product tasks (P.8, C.4) own them.
Largest automatically chosen number of local pipeline workers: a local parallelism setting with identical results at any value.
FASTPQ proof geometry and proof-frame ceilings derived from the transition capacity work_budget.fastpq_default_max_transitions. B.1 and B.2 own the proof-size accounting.
Block cadence and payload retry interval: consensus timing parameters, not resource bounds.
Epoch, demotion, clock-drift and consensus-key lifecycle parameters: validity windows and identities, not bounds on bytes, counts or work.
NPoS staking parameters (the nested `npos` module): economics and schedule, not resource bounds. The committee size on the transport path is transport.max_committee_size.
Metadata nesting depth and the transaction time-to-live: a structural depth and a validity window. Neither bounds bytes, counts or work beyond transaction.max_tx_bytes.
Configuration-parse ceilings of the AXT slot length, clock skew, proof-cache TTL and replay retention: the largest timing window a node may configure. They never meet a transaction.

Hard ceilings applied when node configuration is parsed (parameters/user.rs): the largest value a node may configure for the settlement bound of the same name listed above. A transaction meets the configured value, never the ceiling.
The largest distance between admission and expiry of a settlement bundle, in blocks: a validity window (catalog nexus_consensus_policy_v1 excludes it for the same reason).

Local storage budgets of a Nexus node (hot WSV memory, the enforcement scan interval, the pending evidence peer-key pool) and the retry and backlog limits of its relay worker: process-local pools and schedules that the consensus-policy digest leaves out. Exhausting one defers local work.

Lane fusion and autoscale policy, staking registry capacities and the slash ratio, and DA attester sampling and rotation: lane scheduling, committee and staking policy. The catalog nexus_consensus_policy_v1 excludes the same fields with its reasons.
The number of transactions an authenticated genesis block may carry: a bound of the one bootstrap block, checked when genesis is authenticated. No later block or transaction meets it.

The framed result of the runtime executor shares the VM heap window (guest_memory.heap_max_bytes, which the expression names), and the executor keeps a small cache of runtime variants: an alias of a listed bound and a local cache size.
Sizes of the gossiper's decode and known-hash caches: local caches. A full cache evicts; it never refuses a transaction.

Local cache sizes and the worker-count ceiling of the pipeline (program-hash cache, ZK result cache, automatic worker count), and a gas limit used only by `#[cfg(test)]` items: scheduling and caching that cannot change a result.
Not limits: a list of reserved metadata keys and the text prefix of a rejection reason. Their names contain a limit word.

Local schedule and bookkeeping of the node driver: rejections kept while the executor is busy, the longest idle wait, effects released per poll and heights whose timings are retained. None decides validity.

Read ceilings of the node's own durable records (QC and header metadata, lane frame files, installation-log entries): corruption and allocation guards on local storage, derived from or far above the transport bounds listed above. A refusal is a local storage error, not a verdict.
Evidence proof bytes retained only in this process before admission: a local pool. A full pool defers local reporting and never refuses a block.
An alias: the expression reads block.payload_transaction_reserve_bytes from the data model, which is the listed owner.
How many queued transactions one proposal build inspects: packing policy of the proposer. A transaction beyond the window is inspected by a later build; no block is invalid for what it omits.

Shape bounds of records a block carries beside its transactions: the participant legs of one native AMX claim (255), the canonical frame of one Nexus fee receipt (16 KiB), the leaf count a receipt-proof index can address (2^32, far above block.execution_output_max_outputs) and the signature capacity of a block (the 31 validators of an epoch, below transport.max_committee_size). Each bounds one record inside the block payload limit or the output policy; none is a limit a client's transaction or proof is checked against.

Per-instruction shape limits of product instructions (Parliament sortition batch, MUSUBI pin outbox frames, atomic settlement movements, SoraFS release manifest, election options, pin-allocation fees and frame). Each bounds one instruction of its product; that instruction travels in a transaction bounded by transaction.max_tx_bytes and transaction.max_instructions. The delivery plan assigns these bounds to their product owners.
Not resource bounds: the length a decode-failure placeholder message is truncated to, and the output ceilings of the native wire-ID maintenance tool.

The AEAD expansion of one P2P frame is listed from its configuration owner (transport.aead_frame_overhead_bytes); the length-prefix maximum (u32::MAX) is the wire representation above the runtime ceiling transport.p2p_max_encrypted_frame_bytes.

Local scheduling of one P2P connection and of the network actor: burst sizes per traffic class, drain budgets, batch sizes, buffer and pool capacities, channel capacities, backoff and the trait flag HAS_INBOUND_DECODE_LIMITS. They order and pace delivery. The frame a peer may send is bounded by the transport.* frame bounds; none of these drops a frame the frame bounds admit.

Connection establishment and admission of the P2P layer (handshake payload, DNS answers, proxy response header, first-packet reserve, pending ticket replays, the SoraNet delegation frame and the puzzle work capacities): they bound what a peer may do before or while it is authenticated, not a chain frame.
Limits of the media streaming transport over QUIC (control and media frames, windows, streams, datagram inbox): a separate service of the P2P layer that carries no transaction, block or proof.

The trait constant through which a byte domain states its maximum length. Each implementation is a listed bound (for example rs16.max_availability_frame_bytes and rs16.max_payload_size_bytes), and the comparison in bytes/shared.rs is a recorded site.

Bookkeeping of the consensus machine and the read ceiling of its local safety record: outstanding wants (five reasons), remembered sync sources and the largest safety record a node reads back from its own disk. None is carried in a message or decides validity.

Hardware acceleration policy and calibration of the VM (CPU SHA-2 leaf threshold, CUDA pass budget and provenance file sizes, Metal calibration and discovery budgets and sample sizes) and the native stack of scheduler and prover workers: they choose and time an accelerated path whose result equals the scalar one. Never validity.

Local caches of prepared and decoded programs: their default sizes mirror the listed node-local cache bounds (decoded_scratch.ivm_cache_max_bytes); a full cache evicts and re-decodes, it never refuses a contract.

Geometry of VM components and codecs that the ABI fixes rather than a budget a transaction can approach: the instruction steps of one execution-packet component, the TLV envelope overhead and alignment padding of a host payload, the logical vector length, the decimal scales and limb widths of numeric gas, the default trace length used for padding, a Windows access-mask flag and the list of reserved opcodes.

Limits of host helpers that work on data already inside guest memory or a host payload: the ISO 20022 XML reader, the Ed25519 batch geometry and the state scan candidate count (an alias of the ABI constant). Each bounds one syscall's input, which is bounded by guest_memory.* and charged by work_budget.*; M.1 owns the per-syscall inventory.

Limits of the first-release development state overlay (entries, paths, values and the persisted file): a local tooling store for running contracts off chain. The on-chain value bound is decoded_scratch.state_max_value_bytes.

Shape limits of ABI V1 values a contract builds or decodes inside guest memory (dynamic access hints, query pages, VRF verification requests, JSON construction, lists and aggregate state values). Each bounds one guest structure, which is bounded by guest_memory.heap_max_bytes and decoded_scratch.state_max_value_bytes and charged by work_budget.*. M.1 owns the per-syscall semantic inventory and I.5 the ABI V1 regeneration; they are not bounds between the stages of this path.
Not limits: lists of reserved identifiers and prefixes, the largest register index, the largest first input register of one opcode and two minimum capacities. Their names contain a limit word.

Local diagnostic trace scheduling only: batching, queue capacity and retries do not grant cryptographic proof or ledger authority and are excluded from the consensus-policy hash. Exhaustion delays a diagnostic task.

The standalone polynomial-opening diagnostic endpoint has no ledger relation or registry authority. These finite request bounds can refuse only that local diagnostic request; they do not affect transaction, block or operation-proof admission.
